name: MathlibAnnex.Sphere.radialExtension
title: Radial extension of an isometry between unit spheres

content.display_title: Radial extension of an isometry between unit spheres
content.one_sentence_role: Extends a bijective sphere isometry to all vectors by retaining each radius and transporting its unit direction.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $X,Y$ be real normed spaces, let $S_X=\{x:\|x\|=1\}$ and $S_Y=\{y:\|y\|=1\}$ carry their ambient chord distances, and let $\Delta:S_X\to S_Y$ be a bijective isometry. The radial extension $R_\Delta:X\to Y$ sends zero to zero and sends a nonzero vector to its radius times the image of its unit direction.
content.definition_explanation:
For $x\ne0$, put $\widehat x=\|x\|^{-1}x$. Since $\|x\|>0$,

$$\|\widehat x\|=\|x\|^{-1}\|x\|=1.$$

Thus $\widehat x\in S_X$, so the formula

$$R_\Delta(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x=0,\\ \|x\|\Delta(\widehat x),&x\ne0\end{cases}$$

is well-defined. Normalization fixes unit vectors and is unchanged by positive rescaling, as the cited normalization lemmas state.
content.assumptions: Both spaces are real normed spaces and $\Delta$ is an isometry equivalence of their unit spheres. Neither space is assumed finite-dimensional, complete or nonzero. In the zero space there is no nonzero vector requiring normalization.
content.conclusion: This defines $R_\Delta$ on all of $X$. The separately cited norm theorem gives $\|R_\Delta(x)\|=\|x\|$; for $x\ne0$ this follows from $\|\Delta(x/\|x\|)\|=1$, and zero is immediate. The sphere-agreement theorem gives $R_\Delta(u)=\Delta(u)$ for $u\in S_X$.
content.lean_realization_notes: This is a radial, positively homogeneous extension. Its defining operation uses positive radii; the declaration does not provide a linear extension theorem. In the classification argument $R_\Delta$ is the map used for analytic and topological comparisons; a linear isometry supplied at a later stage is a separate object.
